newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs stay firm on good fundamentals.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Euroyen, JGBs stay firm on good fundamentals.

text.p: SIMEX Euroyen and Japanese government bond (JGB) futures stayed near contract highs on Tuesday as confidence in the Bank of Japan's current monetary policy remained strong, dealers said.
"The fundamentals in Japan are very good," said one Singapore-based dealer.

Dealers said comments on Sunday by Bank of Japan (BOJ) governor Yasuo Matsushita that the fall in long-term interest rates might reflect changing sentiment about Japan's economic prospects remained strongly supportive of both the Euroyen and JGB contracts.
That reinforced hopes for continuing low long-term interest rates, they said.
"People believe short-term rates are going to stay very low, the currency has stabilised and Japan's a good place to park money...it's very bond supportive," the Singapore dealer said.
Euroyen futures contracts moved within very tight trading ranges throughout the day.
March Euroyen ended at 99.24, down from a contract high of 99.25 hit early in the day and a previous IMM close of 99.22.
December JGBs settled at 122.11, down from its opening at 122.14. This compared with the contract's all-time high of 122.60.
Eurodollar futures were particularly quiet all day with most dealers expecting little change ahead of the U.S. non-farm payroll data due out on Friday.

"We're just waiting for Friday." said a local trader. "Some people are looking for tonight's U.S. NAPM (National Association of Purchasing Management index) data but the dominant numbers will be out at the end of the week."
December Eurodollars closed at 94.20, against a previous IMM close of 94.21. March ended at 94.06, against an IMM close of 94.07.
